The theme answers began with “I came”, “I saw”, and “I conquered”, yet when I came to the revealer, not having read its clue, VENI VIDI VICI never entered my mind.  

When I finally read the revealer’s clue, starting with “Classic quotation”, and revealed the first two letters *then* the phrase hit me with a flash and a boom.  

But the English translation in the theme answer clues still hadn’t registered, and thus, when I reread those clues, there came boom number two -- and so for me this was a kapow puzzle.  That pair of booms nixed any nits I might have otherwise had.  I’m a believer.

Little lifts along the way.  The mention of challah evoked its marvelous-to-me look, aroma, and taste.  The contradictory PuzzPair©️ of KEN JENNINGS and DENSE.  Those three-, four-, and five-letter palindromes (AJA, NOON, RADAR).  And the answer AMOR, which backwards adds to the theme VIBE.

Ergo, this was, for me, a splendid outing.  Thank you, Emily and Sala!

People throw the tern "Natick" around lightly, for the intersection of two entries they don't know, when, in fact, the phonotactics of English will limit the options to four or five letters, with one being the most likely. A few weeks ago I gave up on a puzzle, clicked reveal square for the final square (I was that desperate) and I complained that an image showed up which obscured my view of the puzzle altogether.  I could not get rid of it even to see most of my answers.

I have a theory that somehow that image is defaulted when an image can't be found.  On the midi yesterday, there was an image, and on the day of my undoing there was an image in that puzzle as well.

I think sometimes the server can't find an image, and plasters weird thing in its place.  This is often done by browsers and (I think) apps so that something is produced even if an image cannot be found.

I think that's was was happening with my problem, and that's what happened with the mini.

I suspect it gradually went away as more and more servers of the puzzle (they probably have at least a dozen) got the picture in the right place for the app or the web page to find it.

Hi, @lucky13!
As I filled in the clue, I thought of you, and our discussion of color terminology.
Many of our more traditional color terms are actually the terms for the pigments used to produce them--for instance, "azure" is actually the color produced by ground lapis lazuli, which was a very costly pigment.
"Ochre" refers to a whole family of pigments, and thus shades,  based on clays, with varying degrees of iron-rich minerals--limonite, goethite, hematite. There are variants on pigments which have been roasted ("burnt ochre") or not ("raw ochre"). Some are named for the locales where the clays were mined--umber (Umbria), and sienna. So, more complex than our crayola 64-pack would lead us to believe!
And the whole argument whether ochre is "yellow" or "brown" returns us to our basic color terms, and the vague boundaries between them!
